title: El chavalo de al lado
goal: Let a kid teach you the words nobody prints
culture: None of these four words are in a textbook and all four are in every conversation. A nine-year-old will teach them to you faster and more accurately than anybody else, because he has no idea which ones are supposed to be difficult.

beats.good: Chele is what you are: fair, foreign, or both. It is not an insult, it is not going to stop, and the only useful response is to know it.

beats.es: Chele es usted, pues. Blanquito. Pasame ese chunche.
beats.good: A chunche is a thing whose name you do not need: the thingy, the whatsit, that. It will cover about a fifth of everything you cannot yet name.

beats.es: El chunche es... cualquier cosa. Eso. Aquello. ¿Entendiste?
beats.good: Dale is go on, alright, yes, do it. It is the most-used word in the country after pues and on its own it means almost nothing.

beats.objective: Sign off the way he did
beats.good: Vaya pues closes a conversation without ending it. Half the goodbyes in this country are these two words and nothing else.
